summary: Iteration 47 — Cloudflare R2 migration for PLAYER video uploads (Fase A) + verification of the pre-existing .mov→R2 migration (Fase B). 7/8 pytest cases PASS. Fase B (4 pre-migrated reports) fully verified: DB overrides, admin listing, R2 objects, HEAD 200 + video/mp4, and Range→206 all green. Fase A end-to-end (login as testfree-mar, POST /api/reports/upload with real football clip + extracted frame as marker, poll status to 'preview_ready', assert video_url is /api/media/reports/{id}/, HEAD 200 video/mp4, local .web.mp4 removed, R2 object present) PASSES. The single failure is pre-existing seeded data drift (not R2-related): premium@elitescout.com's Lukas A. report references /api/uploads/demo-sample.mp4 which does NOT exist on disk (HTTP 404). The URL routing branch itself is intact — the file is just missing.

minor.issue: Seeded premium user's Lukas A. report has video_url='/api/uploads/demo-sample.mp4' but the file is MISSING from /app/backend/uploads/ — HEAD returns 404. Not a R2-migration bug (the resolver correctly picks the legacy branch when video_url_override is unset). Seed script or a prior cleanup deleted the demo asset. Consider re-uploading demo-sample.mp4 OR migrating this seeded report to R2 by adding a video_url_override.

action_items: Fix the missing demo asset: either restore /app/backend/uploads/demo-sample.mp4 for premium@elitescout.com's Lukas A. seeded report, OR migrate that seeded report to R2 by setting a video_url_override (recommended — same treatment given to the 4 migrated players in Fase B).

/api/media/{key:path} streaming proxy: HEAD returns 200 + content-type video/mp4 + content-length; Range: bytes=0-99 returns 206 with content-range 'bytes 0-99/6413317' — matches R2 spec.

Recommend a follow-up test that pays/manually_unlocks and confirms the video is downloaded from R2 into /tmp for full-report processing.
Cleanup pipeline is solid: after test, DB row is gone (verified via motor async find) and R2 reports/* object count returned to baseline 4 (only the 4 pre-migrated players remain).

Content gate rejection is well-behaved: ffmpeg testsrc + solid-color marker both rejected by Gemini with meaningful analysis_error strings; test now uses the real-football sample /app/backend/uploads/10d5db11-….mp4 with an extracted frame as marker to reach preview_ready.
